threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a ‘tube’ instead of the ‘Overground’ and stand on the wrong side of the escalator. Classic newcomer mistake!
Caught the 45 last night; a guy was singing opera while the driver just sighed. Never a dull moment on these late buses.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Hearing a group of kids yelling ‘ya man!’ at a pigeon while the kebab shop blared Arabic pop. Pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do they have these spontaneous street performances where a random saxophonist joins a tram party at 2 AM. Pure magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they know which taco truck to hit after a night out, no price check needed. They’ve got the green sauce on speed dial.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 21 today and it stopped for a full five minutes because a pigeon was nesting in the rack. Only in the TL.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always rave about the Gaudí buildings, but they miss the hidden murals tucked away in the back streets, which tell our real stories.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewildered faces at the train ticket machines; they still haven’t figured out the quirks of the system.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Tube' instead of just 'the train'—locals rarely bother with the full name.
Saw a guy on the 333 singing full operas. The driver just shook his head and smiled. You wouldn't get that on the day buses!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a hidden garden behind the old brewery on Weserstraße, filled with locals barbecuing and laughing, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand open at 2 AM, serving up greasy goodness to late-night partiers right after the clubs close.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You'll notice the locals refuse to use the term 'Muni' when talking about the bus. They call it 'The 12' or just 'the bus'—it's all about familiarity.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a bus driver shake hands with a regular after helping them get their dog on board. Only in SF do you see that kind of connection in transit.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all shops close in the afternoon, but many in Gràcia reopen for late-night tapas runs. You just have to know where to look.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're recent when they order a café con leche and expect it to come in a to-go cup, totally baffled by the sit-down culture.
